What is the best way to decide rent vs buy?

Process: 1) Calculate total cost of buying (5-7 years), 2) Calculate total cost of renting (5-7 years), 3) Subtract appreciation (estimated 3-4%/year), 4) Subtract opportunity cost (5% return on down payment), 5) Compare. Include: closing costs, maintenance, transaction fees. Most: <5 years, rent. 5-7 years: depends on market. 7+ years: usually buy. Tools: NYT rent vs buy calculator, ours. Most: 5-7 year horizon is the tipping point.
tools.solopreneur-rental-yield-calculato: How do I calculate cash-on-cash return?

CoC = (NOI - debt service) / cash invested. Example: NOI $8K, debt service $5K, cash invested $40K: ($3K) / $40K = 7.5%. Track: total cash invested (down payment + closing + rehab). CoC: 1) Good: 8-12%, 2) Excellent: 12-20%, 3) Top: 20%+. Most investors: target 10%+. CoC varies with leverage. Higher leverage = higher CoC (more risk).
How does rent-to-price ratio affect yield?

Rent-to-price ratio (1% rule) is inverse of yield. 1% monthly = 12% annual gross yield. 0.5% monthly = 6% gross yield. 2% monthly = 24% gross yield. Markets: 0.3% (SF) to 1.5% (Midwest). Higher ratio: better yield, typically less appreciation. Trade-off. Most: 0.7-1% is the sweet spot. Calculate: monthly_rent × 12 / price × 100 = gross yield %.
What is the relationship between yield and appreciation?

Inverse correlation typically. High yield (10%+): less appreciation, often rural/older. Low yield (3-4%): more appreciation, urban/newer. Total return: yield + appreciation. Most markets: 6-10% total. NYC: 3% yield + 5% appreciation = 8% total. Memphis: 8% yield + 2% appreciation = 10% total. Pick: cash flow (yield) or wealth building (appreciation).
What is a good yield for short-term rentals (Airbnb)?

STR yield: typically 1.5-2x higher gross yield than LTR. But: 1) Higher expenses (cleaning, management, utilities), 2) Higher vacancy (off-season), 3) More time-intensive. Net yield: 6-10% typical. Most: 1.0-1.5% monthly gross (12-18% annual gross). For STR DSCR: 1.5+ for lenders. STRs: higher gross but more work. Most investors: 1-2 STR + balance LTR for portfolio.
How do I increase rental yield?

Tactics include 1) Increase rent (market adjustments, value-add), 2) Reduce vacancy (better marketing, faster turn), 3) Reduce expenses (refinance, management optimization), 4) Add income (parking, storage, laundry), 5) Value-add (renovate, add bedrooms). 1-2% yield improvement per year. Most tactics: 0.5-1% gain. Total: 5-10% yield lift achievable. Higher: more risk (higher rent may mean tenant turnover).
tools.solopreneur-arr-multiple-valuation: What is the difference between public and private multiples?

Public SaaS (2026): 8-15x ARR (median ~10x). High growth: 15-25x. Mature: 4-8x. Private rounds: similar but often premium for high growth. Benchmarks: Snowflake peak 100x, now 60x. Datadog: 30x. Cloudflare: 25x. Average public: 10-12x. Average private: 8-15x. Stage: pre-revenue gets 5-10x forward ARR. Most: 8-12x private. Use comparable transactions. Latest deals: most accurate.
How do I justify a higher ARR multiple?

1) Growth: 100%+ YoY, 2) NRR: 120%+, 3) Gross margin: 80%+, 4) Rule of 40: 50%+, 5) Sales efficiency: $1+ ARR per $1 S&M, 6) Payback: <12 months, 7) Logo retention: 95%+, 8) Market: $1B+ TAM. Strong on 3-4 of these: 15-20x. Weak on most: 3-5x. investors pay 2-3x for every 100% growth. Aim for 100%+ growth + 110% NRR = 15-20x.
What is Rule of 40 and why does it matter?

Rule of 40: revenue growth rate + profit margin should be ≥40%. For 60% growth + (-20%) margin: 40% (pass). For 30% growth + 10% margin: 40% (pass). For 100% growth + 0% margin: 100% (great). Investors: rule of 40 is the gold standard for SaaS. Above 40: premium multiple (10-20x). Below 40: discount. Most: aim for 50-80. Top: 80%+. Be honest: it's a balance, not a target.
How do I calculate my own ARR multiple?

For valuation: 1) Calculate ARR, 2) Apply multiple, 3) Result = valuation. For $5M ARR, 10x: $50M. For $20M ARR, 8x: $160M. For benchmarking: 1) Find comparable companies, 2) Average their multiples, 3) Adjust for differences. Sources: public filings, VC databases (PitchBook), comparable transactions. Most: use 3-5 comps. Adjust for growth, retention, market. Be honest: most multiples are 5-10x for healthy SaaS.
What is the impact of gross margin on valuation?

Higher gross margin = higher multiple. SaaS target: 75-85%. Below 60%: 3-5x. 60-75%: 5-10x. 75-85%: 10-15x. 85%+: 15-25x. Why: better unit economics, more profit per dollar, more cash to reinvest. Below 60%: signals services-heavy or low-margin. Most: aim for 80%+. Top: 85%+. Calculate: (revenue - COGS) / revenue. COGS = hosting + support + payment fees. Sales/marketing is opex (not COGS).
tools.solopreneur-burn-multiple-rule-of-: What is a good Burn Multiple for seed stage?

Seed: 1) Pre-PMF: 2-5x (high burn, low ARR), 2) PMF: 1-2x, 3) Growth: 0.5-1x, 4) Series A ready: <1x. aim for 1x by Series A. Top: <0.5x. Avoid >3x (capital inefficient). Track monthly. validate efficiency before raising. Investors: key metric. Capital efficiency: separates good from great. improve 1-2x per year. Aim for <1x by $1-2M ARR.
What is the relationship between Rule of 40 and valuation?

Higher Rule of 40 = higher multiple. Below 40: 3-6x ARR. Above 40: 8-12x. 50-60: 12-18x. 80+: 18-30x. Investors: Rule of 40 is the gate. Above 40: investable. Below: risky. 40-60 is the target. Top: 80+. Use TTM (trailing 12 months). track quarterly. Show: improving trend matters. Most teams 5-10 pp improvement per year.
Can I have a high Rule of 40 with negative margin?

Yes, if growth is high enough. 100% growth + (-50%) margin = 50 (above 40). Investors: accept this for early stage. Trade-off: high growth requires investment. Below 40 with negative margin: bad. Above 40 with negative margin: acceptable early. Above 40 with positive margin: great. Top: positive margin + 30% growth = 40+ (mature). Most: rule of 40 includes both. Use: cash + non-GAAP. Be honest.
How do I calculate Burn Multiple accurately?

Formula: net burn / net new ARR. Net burn = gross burn - revenue. Net new ARR = ending ARR - starting ARR + churn. Track monthly, rolling 12 months. For $100K net burn, $200K net new ARR: 0.5x. quarterly review. Tools: Fathom, Mosaic, custom. Compare: by stage (seed vs Series A). <1x is the goal. Top: <0.5x. Avoid 2x+ (inefficient). Be consistent: methodology matters.
Should Rule of 40 use growth or ARR growth rate?

Either, but specify. ARR growth: 1) YoY (year over year), 2) QoQ (quarter over quarter). Use TTM for stability. YoY TTM. For 50% YoY: 50. For 30% QoQ annualized: 130% (not directly comparable). Investors: prefer TTM YoY. Be consistent. track monthly, show TTM. Avoid 1-month spike (skews). Use trailing 12 months or last 4 quarters. 30%+ YoY + 10%+ margin = 40 (pass).
tools.solopreneur-safe-convertible-note-: What is a discount rate?

Discount: % off next round price. For 20% discount: investor gets shares at 80% of next round price. Combined with cap: investor gets min of (cap or discounted price). 15-25% discount. Common: 20%. For very early: 20-30%. For later: 10-20%. discount + cap is standard. Cap is more important. Most investors: cap is non-negotiable. Discount: less important. Cap drives the economics.
How does a SAFE convert at a priced round?

At priced round: SAFE converts to equity. Calculation: investment / conversion_price. Conversion price = min(price based on cap, price based on discount). For $500K SAFE at $5M cap, 20% discount, $10M priced: 1) Cap: 500K/5M = 10%, 2) Discount: 500K/(10M × 0.8) = 6.25%, 3) Investor gets 10% (cap). Founder dilution: 10% from SAFE. Most: cap is the floor. Discount only matters if no cap or cap is very high.
What is MFN (Most Favored Nation)?

MFN: SAFE gets best terms of any future SAFE. For first SAFE without MFN, second SAFE with better terms: first SAFE still has original terms. With MFN: first SAFE gets the better terms. MFN is investor-friendly. Most SAFEs: include MFN. YC: standard MFN. Trade-off: founder-friendly to exclude (later SAFEs get worse terms). MFN is standard. Avoid no MFN (later SAFEs will demand it anyway).
How much equity does a $500K SAFE at $5M cap give?

Calculate: $500K / $5M cap = 10% of post-money. But: post-money SAFE includes the SAFE itself. For $500K SAFE at $5M cap, $5M round: 1) Post-money = $5M, 2) SAFE = 10%, 3) New investor at $5M post-money = $5M-$500K = $4.5M for new = same 10% if $4.5M price. For YC post-money SAFE: SAFE ownership = investment / cap. So 10% from SAFE. Most: 10% for $500K SAFE at $5M cap. Most: aim for 10-25% dilution per round.
What is the post-money SAFE vs pre-money SAFE?

Pre-money SAFE: cap = pre-money valuation (excludes SAFE). YC post-money SAFE: cap = post-money valuation (includes SAFE). Pre-money: founder-friendly, hard to model. Post-money: investor-friendly, easy to model. Most: post-money SAFE is YC standard (since 2018). For $5M cap post-money: SAFE = 10% immediately. For pre-money $5M: SAFE = 9% (5M/5.5M). Most: 90%+ of SAFEs are now post-money. Use YC standard.
